## Random Variable

Let $(\Omega, \mathcal{F}, P)$ be a probability space. A random variable $X: \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ is measurable when

$$
A_X(x) \triangleq \{\omega \in \Omega : X(\omega) \le x\} = X^{-1}((-
\infty, x]) \in \mathcal{F}.
$$ {#eq-rv}

The set $A_X(x)$ is called a lower level set.

## Distribution function

The CDF is

$$
F_X(x) \triangleq P(X \le x).
$$ {#eq-cdf}

It is non-decreasing, right-continuous, with limits $0$ and $1$ at $-\infty$ and $\infty$.

## Indicator random variable

For an event $A \in \mathcal{F}$, the indicator random variable is

$$
\Ind{A}(\omega) = \begin{cases}
1, & \omega \in A,\\
0, & \omega \notin A.
\end{cases}
$$

## Discrete random variables

If $X$ has countable range, then

$$
X(\omega) = \sum_{x \in \mathcal{X}} x\,\Ind{\{X=x\}}(\omega).
$$

## Continuous random variables

If $X$ has density $f_X$, then

$$
F_X(x) = \int_{-\infty}^x f_X(u)\,du.
$$
